body.x: Tail vein injections and head fixation in animal studies have long relied on the hands of skilled researchers, so results can vary with who performs the procedure.
PLASBIO has taken the route of handing those steps to a vision AI-guided robot, with the aim of making every run repeatable.

PLASBIO Inc., a preclinical research automation company founded in November 2020 and led by CEO Sunggurl Park, builds laboratory automation equipment and AI solutions around that approach. The company is headquartered in Jeonju, Jeonbuk, with a branch in Daejeon, and its goal is to automate biomedical research and standardize the experimental data produced in the preclinical stage.

PLASBIO's main products are the Smart Inject and Brain Inject series, which automate and digitize microinjections and precision experiments on small animals. At the core are on-device automation algorithms that combine AI-based image and motion recognition with precision robotics control. The company automates tail vein injection and stereotaxic head fixation, tasks that previously depended solely on the manual skill of experts, which it says reduces errors tied to researcher skill and improves reproducibility and data reliability. Vision AI detects the condition of the animal in real time and works with the robot.

At KES 2026, PLASBIO is showing its Physical AI-based Microinjection Robot System, an upgraded Smart Inject product, together with a Real-Time Integrated Monitoring Solution that pairs AI-based control software with an intuitive interface. The system automates the microinjection of research models such as cells, embryos and organoids in one all-in-one unit.

The company points to two differentiators. The first is an integrated all-in-one layout that combines the anti-vibration table, robotic arm, display and wiring, previously separate, in a single housing. The second is a vibration reduction design built around a decoupled base, vibration pads and cable management components, which the company says cuts vibration from the 6-axis robotic arm by more than 30%. An adjustable display mount and an AI-based interface complete the design.

PLASBIO is using the show to check the product's technology and design in the global market ahead of its official exhibition at CES 2027. It is also looking for partnerships and new buyers among biopharmaceutical companies, non-clinical contract research organizations (CROs) and research equipment distributors in North America and Europe.

In Korea, PLASBIO supplies its solutions to KAIST, the Korea Research Institute of Bioscience and Biotechnology (KRIBB), the Korea Institute of Toxicology (KIT), Kangwon National University and Chonbuk National University Hospital. The company recorded revenue of KRW 2.1 billion (about USD 1.5 million) in 2025 and aims for KRW 4.6 billion in 2026 by supplying Innovative Procurement Products and expanding deliveries to major institutions.

Overseas, PLASBIO has completed US patent registrations and takes part in NVIDIA Inception and Microsoft's startup support program. It is conducting joint research with Harvard Medical School and the Johns Hopkins Institute for NanoBioTechnology (INBT), is a member of the Chicago-based healthcare innovation institution MATTER and the hard-tech innovation institution mHUB, and was selected in 2026 for the Ministry of Health and Welfare's Research-Driven Hospital Harvard International Cooperation Project. It also took part in the BIO International Convention in 2025 and 2026.

The company's target regions are North America, Europe and Japan. It wants to work with global research equipment distributors that have direct networks with local research institutes and pharmaceutical companies and can provide installation and technical support, and with global non-clinical CROs and large biopharmaceutical companies that would adopt its robots in drug evaluation and help build reference cases. PLASBIO plans to show a new Smart Inject model at CES 2027 and the BIO International Convention 2027, and to raise the share of subscription-based AI data and software revenue as hardware deployments grow. Overseas FDA, CE and ISO certification, which takes time and money, is its main obstacle.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. The show expects 500 exhibitors, 1,100 booths and 70,000 visitors, and its KES Match program holds global buyer meetings on Oct. 14 and Oct. 15 and domestic buyer meetings from Oct. 14 to Oct. 16. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
